newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan coffee production set to dip in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan coffee production set to dip in 1996/97.

text.p: Foul weather and disease will cut coffee output in Uganda in 1996/97 compared to the previous year, the state-owned Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said on Tuesday.

"For the 1996/97 (October/September) year, coffee procurement is estimated at between 3.6 million and 3.8 million 60 kg bags, down from 4.2 million bags realised in the preceding year," UCDA said in a report.

It blamed the drop on the cyclical nature characteristic of perennial crops, a hailstorm in August and September which hit parts of Mubende, Mukono, Mpigi and Kiboga affecting plantations, and coffee wilt disease in some districts.
Uganda's main coffee districts are just outside Kampala, an in the central, eastern and southwestern parts of the country.
Uganda is Africa's leading producer of coffee, which earns it around 70 percent of all foreign currency revenues.
Some 90 percent of Uganda's coffee is of the robusta variety while only 12 percent is of the better paying arabicas.
UCDA said the main harvesting season in the southwestern region was almost coming to an end and coffee buyers were gradually shifting their activities to the central and eastern regions.
"The heavy rains during the month of October delayed both harvesting and trading activities," UCDA said.
